# Guide to FAIR

## Overview

This guide provides practical guidance on applying the [FAIR principles](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/) to [Bioconductor](https://www.bioconductor.org/) materials. It considers how software, data, and training resources can be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable within and beyond the Bioconductor ecosystem.

As part of the Bioconductor community, we develop and maintain open-source software, data, and training resources. This guide supports users and developers in making those resources easier to discover, access, integrate, and reuse within and beyond the Bioconductor ecosystem.

## FAIR Bioconductor functionality

The following sections will develop processes, resources, and checklists for producing FAIR Bioconductor tool wrappers and workflows, including integrations with Galaxy and nf-core.

## What this guide is not

This guide does not replace the documentation and guidance maintained by the Galaxy and nf-core communities for:

- [Tool development and integration into Galaxy](https://training.galaxyproject.org/training-material/topics/dev/tutorials/tool-integration/slides-plain.html)
- [Creating nf-core modules](https://nf-co.re/docs/nf-core-tools/cli/modules/create)

It signposts to these resources where appropriate while focusing on the FAIR aspects of integrating Bioconductor functionality.

## Interoperable file types

Preferred file types for disk-based storage of R objects and interoperability with other programming languages and software ecosystems will be documented here.
